parts.latex:
City $A$ is at latitude $34^\circ$S and longitude $151^\circ$E. City $B$ is $72^\circ$ north of City $A$ and $25^\circ$ west of City $A$.

What are the latitude and longitude of City $B$?

solutions.latex:
City $A$ is at $34^\circ$S. Moving $72^\circ$ north crosses the equator after $34^\circ$, with $72^\circ - 34^\circ = 38^\circ$ left over.
$$\text{Latitude of } B = 38^\circ\text{N}$$
Moving $25^\circ$ west decreases the longitude from $151^\circ$E.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Longitude of } B &= 151^\circ - 25^\circ \\ &= 126^\circ\text{E} \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

meta.generated_note: MCQ working written from the answer key.

parts.latex:
Johnny is travelling from Oslo, Norway ($60^\circ$ N, $11^\circ$ E) to Perth, Australia ($32^\circ$ S, $116^\circ$ E).

Including a stopover, Johnny takes 28 hours to travel from Oslo to Perth.

Given that Johnny leaves Oslo at 8 am on Tuesday, what is the local time and day when Johnny arrives in Perth?

solutions.latex:
Oslo is on UTC+1 and Perth on UTC+8, so the time difference is $7$ hours.

Alternatively, the longitude difference is $116^\circ - 11^\circ = 105^\circ$, and
$$\dfrac{105^\circ}{15^\circ} = 7 \text{ h}$$
Take-off: Oslo 8 am Tuesday, which is Perth 3 pm Tuesday.

Landing, 28 hours later: Oslo 12 pm Wednesday, London 11 am Wednesday, Perth 7 pm Wednesday.
$$\therefore\ \text{Johnny arrives at 7 pm Wednesday (Perth time)}$$
criteria: Correct time difference and one correct take-off or landing time, or equivalent merit
Correct time difference of $7$ h, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
City $A$ is in Sweden and is located at $(58^\circ\text{N}, 16^\circ\text{E})$. Sydney, in Australia, is located at $(33^\circ\text{S}, 151^\circ\text{E})$.

Robert lives in Sydney and needs to give an online presentation to his colleagues in City $A$ starting at 5:00 pm Thursday, local time in Sweden.

What time and day, in Sydney, should Robert start his presentation?

It is given that $15^\circ = 1$ hour time difference. Ignore daylight saving.

solutions.latex:
Both cities have longitude to the East.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Longitude difference} &= 151^\circ - 16^\circ \\ &= 135^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Time difference} &= 135\div 15 \\ &= 9 \text{ hours} \end{aligned}$$
Sydney is further east, so it is 9 hours ahead of City $A$.

$\therefore$ The time in Sydney is 2 am Friday.
criteria: Calculates time difference, or equivalent merit
Calculates longitude difference, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
During the 2000 Olympic Games in Sydney, which is located at $(35^\circ\text{S}, 150^\circ\text{E})$, the 100 m freestyle swimming final was held on a Wednesday at 2:00 pm local time. The event was broadcast live to New York, which is located at $(40^\circ\text{N}, 75^\circ\text{W})$.

What time and day was the event broadcast in New York?

It is given that $15^\circ = 1$ hour time difference. Ignore daylight saving.

solutions.latex:
The longitude difference is found by adding, since the cities are on opposite sides of $0^\circ$.
$$\text{Longitude difference}=75+150=225^\circ$$
$$\text{Time difference}=225\div 15=15\text{ hours}$$
New York is west of Sydney, so it is 15 hours behind Sydney.
$$2\text{ pm}-15\text{ hours}=11{:}00\text{ pm}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the event was broadcast at 11:00 pm on Tuesday.}$$
criteria: Finds the time difference and subtracts it, or equivalent merit
Finds the longitude difference, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Cairo in Egypt is located at $(30^\circ\text{N},\ 31^\circ\text{E})$.

Sydney, in Australia, is located at $(33^\circ\text{S},\ 151^\circ\text{E})$.

Camilla lives in Sydney and needs to attend an online meeting with her business partners in Cairo starting at 11:00 am on Monday, local time in Cairo.

What time and day, in Sydney, does Camilla need to log on to the meeting?

Ignore daylight saving.

solutions.latex:
Time zones are based on longitude: each $15^\circ$ is 1 hour, and places further east are ahead.

The difference in longitude is

$$151^\circ - 31^\circ = 120^\circ$$
So the time difference is

$$\dfrac{120}{15} = 8 \text{ hours}$$
Sydney is further east, so Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Cairo.

Cairo 11:00 am Monday becomes

$$11{:}00 \text{ am} + 8 \text{ h} = 7{:}00 \text{ pm Monday}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Camilla must log on at 7:00 pm on Monday (Sydney time).}$$
criteria: Finds the time difference of 8 hours, or equivalent merit
Finds the difference in longitude of $120^\circ$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A cruise ship left Sydney ($34^\circ\text{S}, 151^\circ\text{E}$) to travel to the island of Desmos.

When the ship arrived in Desmos, it was $72^\circ$ north and $124^\circ$ west of Sydney.

What is the location of Desmos?

solutions.latex:
Sydney is $34^\circ\text{S}$, so moving $72^\circ$ north gives latitude
$$\begin{aligned} -34 + 72 &= 38 \\ &= 38^\circ\text{N} \end{aligned}$$
Sydney is $151^\circ\text{E}$, so moving $124^\circ$ west gives longitude
$$\begin{aligned} 151 - 124 &= 27 \\ &= 27^\circ\text{E} \end{aligned}$$
Hence Desmos is at $(38^\circ\text{N}, 27^\circ\text{E})$, option A.

parts.latex:
The coordinates of Tokyo are $(36^\circ\text{N}, 140^\circ\text{E})$ and the coordinates of Oslo are $(60^\circ\text{N}, 11^\circ\text{E})$.

If the sun rises at 7 am in Oslo, what time will it be in Tokyo when the sun rises in Oslo? You may assume $15^\circ = 1$ hour.

solutions.latex:
Time difference depends only on the difference in longitude. Both cities are in the eastern hemisphere, so subtract the longitudes.
$$\begin{aligned} 140^\circ-11^\circ &= 129^\circ \\ \text{time difference} &= \dfrac{129}{15} \\ &= 8.6 \text{ hours} \\ &= 8 \text{ h } 36 \text{ min} \end{aligned}$$
Tokyo is further east, so its time is ahead of Oslo's.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Tokyo time} &= 7:00 \text{ am}+8\text{ h }36\text{ min} \\ &= 3:36 \text{ pm} \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

meta.generated_note: Latitude is irrelevant to time difference.

parts.latex:
$P\,(30^\circ\text{S}, 100^\circ\text{E})$ is a point on the Earth's surface.

Give the coordinates of the point which is $40^\circ$ North and $40^\circ$ West of point $P$.

solutions.latex:
Moving $40^\circ$ North from $30^\circ\text{S}$ gives $10^\circ\text{N}$.

Moving $40^\circ$ West from $100^\circ\text{E}$ gives $60^\circ\text{E}$.

So the point is $(10^\circ\text{N}, 60^\circ\text{E})$, which is option B.

parts.latex:
City $A$ is in Sweden and is located at ($58^\circ$N, $16^\circ$E).

Sydney, in Australia, is located at ($33^\circ$S, $151^\circ$E).

Robert lives in Sydney and needs to give an online presentation to his colleagues in City $A$ starting at 5:00 pm Thursday, local time in Sweden.

What time and day, in Sydney, should Robert start his presentation?

It is given that $15^\circ = 1$ hour time difference. Ignore daylight saving.

solutions.latex:
Find the difference in longitude.
$$151^\circ - 16^\circ = 135^\circ$$
Using $15^\circ = 1$ hour:
$$\text{time difference} = 135 \div 15 = 9 \text{ hours}$$
Sydney is east of City $A$, so Sydney is 9 hours ahead.

Adding 9 hours to 5:00 pm Thursday gives the Sydney time.
$$\therefore\ \text{Robert should start at 2:00 am Friday.}$$
criteria: Finds the time difference, or equivalent merit
Finds the difference in longitude, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: The coordinates of Dublin are $(53^\circ\text{N}, 6^\circ\text{W})$. What are the coordinates of Hamburg if it is $16^\circ$ East of Dublin?

solutions.latex:
Dublin is at $6^\circ\text{W}$. Moving $16^\circ$ east gives
$$-6^\circ + 16^\circ = 10^\circ\text{E}$$
The latitude is unchanged.
$$\therefore\ \text{Hamburg is } (53^\circ\text{N}, 10^\circ\text{E})$$

parts.latex: What is the time difference between world cities with co-ordinates $(20^\circ\text{S},\ 45^\circ\text{E})$ and $(20^\circ\text{S},\ 105^\circ\text{E})$?

solutions.latex:
The difference in longitude is $105^\circ-45^\circ=60^\circ$.

Since $15^\circ$ corresponds to 1 hour, $60^\circ$ corresponds to 4 hours.

Hence the answer is option D.

parts.latex:
San Francisco is located at $(38^\circ\text{N}, 122^\circ\text{W})$. City $X$ is located $40^\circ$ to the South and $50^\circ$ to the East of San Francisco.

What are the coordinates of City $X$?

solutions.latex:
Moving $40^\circ$ south decreases the latitude:
$$38^\circ\text{N} - 40^\circ = -2^\circ, \text{ which is } 2^\circ\text{S}$$
Moving $50^\circ$ east decreases the west longitude:
$$122^\circ\text{W} - 50^\circ = 72^\circ\text{W}$$
So City $X$ is at $(2^\circ\text{S}, 72^\circ\text{W})$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the answer is option D}$$

parts.latex:
Sydney is at the coordinates $34^\circ\text{S}, 151^\circ\text{E}$, and Tokyo is at the coordinates $36^\circ\text{N}, 140^\circ\text{E}$.

What is the time difference, to the nearest minute, between Sydney and Tokyo?

solutions.latex:
Each $15^\circ$ of longitude is 1 hour, so each $1^\circ$ is 4 minutes. The difference in longitude is $151-140=11^\circ$.
$$\text{Time difference}=11\times4=44\text{ minutes}$$
Sydney is $44$ minutes ahead of Tokyo.
criteria: Finds the difference in longitude, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Four cities have the following locations:

Sydney $(34^\circ S,151^\circ E)$ Manila $(15^\circ N,121^\circ E)$

Hawaii $(20^\circ N,156^\circ W)$ Canberra $(35^\circ S,149^\circ E)$

On New Year's Eve, which city will be first to enter the New Year?

solutions.latex:
The Earth rotates towards the east, so places further east reach midnight earlier. The city furthest east in longitude is first to enter the New Year (latitude does not matter).

The longitudes are:
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Sydney} &: 151^\circ \text{E} \\ \text{Manila} &: 121^\circ \text{E} \\ \text{Hawaii} &: 156^\circ \text{W} \\ \text{Canberra} &: 149^\circ \text{E} \end{aligned}$$
Hawaii is in the western hemisphere, so it is last. Among the eastern cities, $151^\circ \text{E}$ is the largest.

Hence Sydney is first, option A.

meta.self_check: Compared longitudes; Sydney 151E is most easterly before the date line (Hawaii at 156W is 204E-equivalent but is behind the date line, so is later).
